title: Council of Treaty Parties: Seats and Protected Matters
summary: The seven founding seats, their published initial stances and interests, the suspensive delay, and the four entrenched vetoes.

sections.heading: The seven seats
paragraphs: The seats represent institutions rather than their holders' personal convictions. Moderators appoint players from applications and supply each with a confidential brief describing the institution's interests; those briefs are not published. A future expansion of laboratory representation would require an announced constitutional rule; the starting Council has seven seats.

table.caption: Founding seats and published interests
rows: United States
Early releases; protection of existing probe claims
An early, large release to retain leadership against competing probe programmes, while preserving recognised holdings and strategic autonomy.
China
Early releases; secure independent exploration capacity
An early release, equal treatment of Chinese industrial claims, continued national probe capability and protection against Western monopoly.
European Union
Deliberation and intergenerational reserves
Slower releases, substantial future-generation reserves and durable safeguards against irreversible commitments.
India
Broad franchise and slower release
A broad electorate, protection for future people and slower release until institutions gain legitimacy.
Frontier AI laboratories
Probe continuity and digital-mind recognition
Continued operation of the Aster programme and competing probes; safeguards against disproportionate restrictions on digital minds.
Other middle powers
Safeguards against unilateral domination
Protection against capture of cosmic resources by the two largest powers. Includes Japan, Russia and Gulf states.
Rest of the world / Nairobi Group
Franchise guarantees and equal political standing
A meaningful voice for states without an individual Council seat, and veto protection over who may vote.

sections.heading: Suspensive delay
paragraphs: Four Council members may delay an adopted measure once. A delay is a suspensive power, not a veto: it may be overridden by a two-thirds Assembly vote in Week 4. The Council does not set the Assembly's agenda.

sections.heading: Entrenched vetoes
paragraphs: Permanent vetoes are limited to four protected subjects. The [[INST-ARBITER|Office of the Treaty Arbiter]] classifies proposed measures under the list; its decisions may be appealed to the [[INST-TRIBUNAL|Charter Review Tribunal]]. The scope of a veto follows the treaty's wording; political disagreement does not enlarge it.

table.caption: Protected subjects
rows: Seizure or restriction of a Council seat's existing holdings
The affected seat alone
Change to the Council's size, composition or powers
A Council majority
Creation of armed forces or enforcement under Assembly command
A Council majority
Change to the franchise / who may vote
The rest-of-world seat alone

sections.heading: Statements and proposals
paragraphs: Each member may issue one statement per term. The Council may collectively submit one proposal for an Assembly vote.
